ticker: Quotes for the S&P 500, NASDAQ Composite, VIX, MSCI World and WTI crude, plus 20 watchlist stocks, and the fed funds rate.
daychange: Today's percent change for every S&P 500 stock.
breadth: Daily prices for every S&P 500 stock, to count advances and declines, new highs and lows, and the share above the 200-day average.
drawdown: Full daily price history for SPY and URTH.
sectors: Daily prices for the 11 SPDR sector ETFs and SPY, and the 11 Invesco equal-weight sector ETFs and RSP.
ath-tradingview: Which S&P 500 stocks are at an all-time high, from TradingView's screener.
countries: Daily prices for country and region ETFs, plus a value and growth pair.
seasonality: Full daily history of the S&P 500 index.
putcall: Put/call ratio history and daily prices. No page of its own: feeds the Sentiment Index through the sentiment job.
sentiment: Daily prices from Yahoo Finance for the S&P 500, VIX, VIX3M, SKEW, Russell 2000, long Treasuries, high-yield and investment-grade bonds and RSP (history back to 1990), plus the breadth job's results, scored into the composite. The put/call ratio and news sentiment scores are published alongside it but not scored.
oddstats: Daily history for the S&P 500, SPY, the 11 sector ETFs and 25 mega-caps, to scan for streaks.
smallcap: Daily prices for IWM (small caps), MDY (mid caps) and SPY (large caps).
beeswarm-daily: 15-minute price moves through the trading day for every S&P 500 stock.
international: Daily prices for EFA (developed markets), EEM (emerging markets) and SPY, plus the EUR/USD rate.
concentration: Monthly prices and SEC share counts for the Magnificent Seven stocks.
concentration-history: Long-history index data for the top-10 share of the S&P 500.
factors: Fama-French daily factor returns, back to 1926.
beeswarm-meta: Name, sector and shares outstanding for every S&P 500 stock. Company names and sectors reused by about 20 other jobs.
beeswarm-annual: Year-by-year returns for the 11 sector ETFs and SPY, about 15 years.
revisions: Analyst EPS estimates for the current year and how they moved over 7, 30 and 90 days.
post-earnings-drift: About ten years of S&P 500 earnings reports from the shared earnings collection, with Yahoo prices: the reaction around each report and the drift over the next 20 and 60 trading days, by size of surprise, plus the latest quarter's reports. No Alpha Vantage calls.
relative-strength: Daily prices for every S&P 500 stock and SPY, for 1-month and 3-month relative strength.
smallcap-liquidity: Daily prices and volume for about 200 large and small stocks.
short-sale-volume: Daily short-sale volume from FINRA, plus daily prices.
valuations: Monthly S&P 500 valuation multiples by sector and industry (trailing and forward P/E, EV/EBITDA, price/book, price/sales) and a rebuilt ten-year history of trailing P/E. Reads the overview and earnings collections refreshed just before it, plus Yahoo prices, so it makes no Alpha Vantage calls.
short-interest: FINRA's twice-monthly short interest for past and present S&P 500 members since June 2021. Each run stores any new settlement dates and rebuilds the page data when one arrives, or once a week. Shares outstanding come from the shared company overviews, prices from Yahoo, so it makes no Alpha Vantage calls.
analyst-price-target: Analyst price target and buy, hold and sell ratings for every S&P 500 stock.
earnings-growth-divergence: Earnings history for every S&P 500 stock, compared with price performance.
equity-risk-premium: Company overviews for every S&P 500 stock, plus Treasury yields.
margin-leverage: Income statements and balance sheets for every S&P 500 stock, plus the fed funds rate. Two runs finish one cycle: the sweep is too long for one 15-minute run, so each run saves progress and the next resumes.
quality-financials: Annual balance sheet and income figures for every S&P 500 stock. Makes no API calls: reads the annual reports margin-leverage already saved.
quality-score: Cash flow for every S&P 500 stock, added to the financials for a quality score. Second stage of the Quality Score page. Needs quality-financials first.
surprise: Reported versus estimated earnings for every S&P 500 stock. Manual snapshot. Post-earnings-drift depends on it.
volatility: Full daily history of the S&P 500 index and the VIX since 1990, plus the VIX9D, VIX3M and VIX6M indices for the term structure.
concentration-market: Daily prices for SPY and RSP.
backtest-prices: Daily prices for whatever symbol you enter.
options-positioning: Put/call ratio for every S&P 500 stock, joined against the relative-strength history for the momentum test.
overview-collector: One sweep of company overviews (name, sector, share count, P/E, analyst targets and ratings, dividend yield, beta, 52-week range, moving averages, insider and institutional ownership, industry, EBITDA, EV/EBITDA, price/book, revenue) for every S&P 500 stock, saved for other jobs to read. Runs on the 2nd of each month, with a second run 25 minutes later to finish a sweep that ran out of time.
earnings-collector: One sweep of earnings history (reported and estimated EPS, surprise) for every S&P 500 stock, saved for other jobs to read. Runs on the 2nd of each month, with a second run 25 minutes later to finish a sweep that ran out of time.
cashflow-collector: One sweep of quarterly and annual cash flow (including buybacks, dividends and stock-based compensation) for every S&P 500 stock, saved for other jobs to read.
estimates-collector: One sweep of analyst EPS estimates for every S&P 500 stock, saved for other jobs to read.
income-collector: One sweep of quarterly and annual income statements for every S&P 500 stock, saved for other jobs to read.
balance-collector: One sweep of quarterly and annual balance sheets for every S&P 500 stock, saved for other jobs to read.
putcall-history: Put/call ratio of every S&P 500 member at each month-end for the last five years, plus one current snapshot each week, for the put/call ratio page's forward-return study, and weekly put/call ratios for SPY, QQQ and IWM since 2008 for the Options Positioning page. The backfill runs in short overnight batches.
putcall-study: Builds the put/call ratio page from the put/call snapshots: this week's highest and lowest ratios with analyst ratings and trailing returns, and what followed extreme readings at each month-end. Reads the shared company overviews and Yahoo prices, so it makes no Alpha Vantage calls.
